findings.title: Memory limit has no unit, so it is in bytes
findings.cause: container api's memory limit is memory: 512, which Kubernetes reads as 512 bytes: the kubelet sizes the pod's memory-backed volumes by that limit, so it cannot even write the service account token into one (no space left on device), and the pod never starts; Deployment api has 0 of 1 replicas ready

evidence.detail: (combined from similar events): MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "kube-api-access-vgfdc" : write /var/lib/kubelet/pods/3d520dde-fa6d-4837-8148-6cba5ab919ca/volumes/kubernetes.io~projected/kube-api-access-vgfdc/..2026_11_25_16_08_50.1671447070/ca.crt: no space left on device

evidence.what: container api's memory limit is 512, with no unit

findings.fix: Give the limit a unit: 512Mi if mebibytes were meant (Mi and Gi are powers of 1024; M and G are powers of 1000), and the request the same way.
